summary: Montmorency County, MI lookout also called Atlanta East; listed as removed and down. Forest Lookouts gives a 1921 steel tower, but its link to this site is not confirmed.

facts.status_note: Michigan Fire Towers lists the tower as removed and down, with no removal date and no description of the site

events.note: Forest Lookouts Atlanta entry: a steel tower was erected (per the 1922 Biennial Report). Not confirmed as this East tower

evidence.supports: tower is also known as Atlanta East Fire Tower; alias East Atlanta Fire Tower
evidence.quote: Tower Name: Atlanta East Fire Tower

evidence.supports: tower is listed as removed and down
a steel tower was erected in 1921
the 1921 entry cites the Department of Conservation biennial report of 1922
evidence.quote: Biennial Report - The Department of Conservation - 1922

evidence.supports: a 1937 item describes a 60-foot tower about 10 miles north of Atlanta being replaced
evidence.quote: The latest 60-footer to go is the one about 10 miles north of Atlanta in Montmorency county.

evidence.supports: replacement by a 100-foot tower built by CCC men from Camp Presque Isle
evidence.quote: A 100 foot fire tower is being erected by CCC men from Camp Presque Isle to take its place.

evidence.supports: the 1937 item is from the Lake County Star
OpenStreetMap node is named Atlanta Lookout Tower
elevation 309 metres recorded on the OpenStreetMap node
the Lake County Star item is dated May 28, 1937

notes_for_editor: Thin sources. Michigan Fire Towers gives PID QK0616, Removed: Yes, Status: Down, and T. Cabin: no (abbreviation unclear; not used in the story). The Forest Lookouts Atlanta entry does not name which Atlanta tower its 1921 steel tower refers to, so the 1921 build event is flagged as unconfirmed. The 1937 item describes a 60-foot tower about 10 miles north of Atlanta, not this site. The record height of 18.3 m (60 ft) has no source read that supports it for this tower; left out of facts. Removal date and current site condition unknown. A web search found no page on this tower. Suggested follow-up: Michigan DNR Atlanta-unit fire tower records and local historical society files.
